title: Evening Node Load Leads to Unstable Nimbus Fibre Service
symptoms: Websites become unresponsive after a few minutes
Streaming video pauses frequently
Online gaming shows lag spikes
Wi-Fi connection drops intermittently
Email client fails to send or receive at times

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the connectivity issue observed primarily after 6 pm?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Proceed to check node utilization during peak hours

diagnostic_questions.q: Do multiple devices on the same premises experience the problem simultaneously?
Has the customer reported similar issues on consecutive evenings?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Strengthen case for congestion-related root cause

steps.text: Access the provisioning portal and confirm the customer's MAC address is correctly registered and not flagged for bandwidth throttling; outcome: assurance that account settings are correct
Open the network management system (NMS) and locate the shared node serving the customer's address; outcome: node identified for performance review
Review the node's utilization graphs for the 18:00-22:00 window over the past 7 days; outcome: visibility of peak load patterns
If average utilization exceeds the 85 % threshold, document the overload and initiate a capacity-upgrade request; outcome: plan to alleviate congestion
If utilization is within normal limits, run a remote optical line test (OLT) to capture Rx/Tx power levels and signal-to-noise ratio; outcome: confirmation of physical layer health
Compare measured optical metrics against the acceptable range (Rx - 3 dBm to - 8 dBm, Tx - 2 dBm to - 6 dBm); outcome: determination whether signal degradation exists
For out-of-spec results, generate a field-technician ticket with detailed test data; outcome: on-site investigation scheduled

escalate_when: Node utilization remains above 85 % for three consecutive evenings despite no remediation
Optical signal levels are out of spec after multiple remote tests
Customer reports the same instability across all devices and browsers for more than 48 hours
notes: Evening congestion on shared nodes is a common cause of intermittent performance for Nimbus Fibre. Document all timestamps and test results in the ticket to aid engineering analysis. If a capacity upgrade is approved, communicate the expected timeline to the customer and set a follow-up reminder.
root_cause: evening congestion on the shared node

title: Intermittent service disruption on Nimbus ONT-5G - possible fibre line impairment
symptoms: Web pages load slowly then stop responding
Video streams pause or buffer frequently
Online games lag or disconnect
Wi-Fi seems fine but wired devices lose connectivity
Ping times jump dramatically

diagnostic_questions.q: Are any of the ONT-5G status LEDs flickering or showing red?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Proceed to check the fiber cable condition

diagnostic_questions.q: Has any construction or digging occurred near your premises in the last week?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Note possible external damage and proceed with caution

diagnostic_questions.q: Do you see the optical power reading within the normal range on the ONT dashboard?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Line quality likely OK, continue troubleshooting

steps.text: Confirm the ONT-5G is receiving power and note the state of all LEDs; green steady indicates normal operation, amber/red indicates an issue.
Visually inspect the incoming fiber cable and the connector at the ONT for bends, kinks, or visible contamination.
If contamination is suspected, clean the fiber connector using a lint-free wipe and a certified fiber cleaning tool, following the manufacturer's procedure.
Log into the ONT web UI and record the current optical power level; compare it to the device's acceptable range (-28 dBm to -8 dBm typical).
Initiate a remote OTDR trace or perform a local loopback test to identify attenuation spikes or reflections indicative of a faulty splice or connector.
If the power reading is outside the normal range or the OTDR shows high loss at the connector, replace the fiber patch cord with a new, certified cable.
Perform a soft reset of the ONT via the UI (or press the reset button briefly) and monitor the LEDs and service stability for at least 15 minutes.
Document all observations, actions taken, and the final status; close the ticket if the service remains stable, otherwise move to escalation.

escalate_when: Optical power remains out of spec after cleaning and cable replacement
LEDs continue to flash red or amber after soft reset
Customer reports more than three service drops within an hour despite completed steps
notes: Line-level noise or a degraded fibre connector can cause sporadic loss of signal even when the ONT appears powered. Cleaning or replacing the connector often restores the optical budget. If the issue persists, a field technician may need to inspect the distribution fiber or splice points.
root_cause: line noise or a degraded fibre connector

title: Intermittent connectivity on Nimbus Fibre - ONT firmware issue
symptoms: The internet works for a few minutes then drops out
Web pages load slowly or time out intermittently
Streaming video pauses and buffers repeatedly
Online games experience sudden lag spikes

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the ONT showing a blinking red status LED?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Check for external line faults first

diagnostic_questions.q: Does the customer report the same issue after power-cycling the ONT?
Is the ONT firmware version older than 2.5.1?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Skip upgrade and move to next step

steps.text: Ask the customer to locate the ONT and note the model number and current firmware version displayed on the web-interface or LCD panel.
Log into the NMS and verify the ONT's firmware version against the latest release; record the version in the ticket.
If the firmware is outdated, push the latest stable firmware package (e.g., 2.5.3) to the ONT via the remote upgrade function and confirm successful installation.
After the upgrade, have the customer perform a controlled test: browse several websites and run a speed test for at least 5 minutes, noting any drops.
If the connection remains unstable, reset the ONT to factory defaults, re-apply the customer's VLAN and QoS settings, and re-provision the device from the NMS.
Monitor the ONT for 30 minutes; ensure the status LEDs remain solid green and no error logs appear.
Document the firmware version, upgrade timestamps, and test results in the ticket before closing.

escalate_when: Firmware version is older than the minimum supported release and upgrade fails
Instability persists after successful firmware upgrade and reset
Multiple subscribers on the same distribution node report identical symptoms
notes: This article addresses the known firmware defect that causes sporadic link drops on certain ONT revisions. Ensure the upgrade is performed during a low-traffic window to minimise impact.

title: Intermittent connection on Nimbus ONT-5G caused by Wi-Fi channel congestion
symptoms: Web pages load slowly then stop responding
Video streams pause or buffer unexpectedly
Online games lag or disconnect mid-match
Smart home devices lose connectivity sporadically

diagnostic_questions.q: Are there several other wireless networks visible on the same floor?
Is the ONT-5G placed near a microwave oven, cordless phone base, or Bluetooth hub?

steps.text: Log into the Nimbus ONT-5G management console via its local IP address.
Navigate to the Wi-Fi settings page and note the current 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz channel numbers.
Open a Wi-Fi analyzer tool on a laptop or smartphone; scan the surrounding spectrum and record the channel utilization percentages for each overlapping channel.
If any channel shows >30 % utilization, change the ONT-5G to a less-congested channel (or set the channel selection to 'Auto' for dynamic adjustment).
For the 5 GHz band, enable a wider channel width (e.g., 40 MHz) only if the analyzer shows low neighboring traffic; otherwise keep it at 20 MHz to reduce overlap.
Apply the new settings and verify that the signal strength (RSSI) on client devices is ≥-70 dBm.
Ask the customer to perform a 5-minute streaming test on a device; confirm that playback remains smooth without pauses.
Document the channel changes and outcomes in the ticket before closing.

escalate_when: The issue persists after changing to a clear channel on both bands
Signal strength remains below -70 dBm despite optimal placement
Multiple devices still experience drops after the above steps
notes: If the ONT-5G firmware is older than version 3.2, schedule a firmware upgrade before performing channel adjustments, as older firmware may have limited channel selection logic.

title: Nimbus Fibre - Complete service outage (local node failure)
symptoms: I can't load any web pages on any device.
All my lights are off or flashing red on the fibre terminal.
My phone says 'No internet connection' even though Wi-Fi is connected.
Streaming video just buffers forever.
The speed test shows 0 Mbps.

diagnostic_questions.q: Are any neighbours reporting the same loss of service?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Proceed to check local node status in NOC tools.

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the Power LED on the ONT solid green?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Ask customer to confirm power is plugged in and advise power cycle.

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the Ethernet port on the ONT showing link activity?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Check fiber connector and reseat if necessary.

steps.text: Confirm the customer's address and service ID in the ticketing system.
Access the NOC dashboard for the customer's distribution node and verify node status; expected outcome: node appears online or offline.
Check remote telemetry for ONT LEDs: Power LED solid green and LOS LED off indicate proper power and no loss of signal.
Instruct the customer to ensure the ONT is plugged in and the fiber connector is securely seated; expected outcome: ONT LEDs change to normal operating pattern.
Issue a remote ONT reset via the management console; expected outcome: ONT reboots and attempts to re-sync with the network.
Monitor the ONT sync status for up to 2 minutes; if sync is achieved, verify downstream traffic by pinging a public DNS; expected outcome: internet connectivity restored.
If sync is not achieved, create a back-haul node escalation ticket for physical inspection; expected outcome: issue escalated to field engineering.

escalate_when: If the NOC dashboard shows the local node still offline after remote reset.
If multiple customers in the same node are affected.
If the ONT does not achieve sync after two remote resets.
notes: Local node failures often require field technician intervention. Record all telemetry timestamps and inform the customer of the estimated time to repair based on current field crew availability.

title: Complete service loss - Nimbus ONT-5G (fibre cut)
symptoms: No internet connectivity on any device
All indicator lights on the ONT are off or amber
Web pages fail to load
Speed test reports 0 Mbps
Wi-Fi network not broadcasting

diagnostic_questions.q: Are any of the ONT status LEDs solid green?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Likely loss of upstream signal; continue troubleshooting

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the ONT receiving power (power LED on)?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Ask customer to verify power connection or replace power adapter

diagnostic_questions.q: Do other customers on the same street report service issues?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Issue may be localized to premises

steps.text: Confirm the ONT is plugged into a working outlet and that the power LED is illuminated; outcome: ONT powers up and shows initial boot sequence
Visually inspect the fiber connector for a loose plug or visible damage; outcome: connector is firmly seated and no obvious physical defect
Log into the ONT admin portal and read the Optical Power and Link Status values; outcome: Link status shows "Down" and power level is out of the acceptable range
Query the NOC dashboard for any reported fiber incidents in the affected area; outcome: either a confirmed external cut or no reported fault
If the NOC confirms a cut, create an incident ticket, schedule repair crew, and provide the customer with an estimated restoration time; outcome: ticket logged and customer informed
If no external incident is logged, initiate the ONT's built-in loopback test (if supported); outcome: test result indicates line fault when it fails
Replace the ONT with a spare unit and repeat steps 1-3; outcome: new ONT should acquire a stable link; if still down, the fault is likely upstream
Document all findings and, if the problem persists, escalate to the engineering team; outcome: escalation record created for deeper analysis

escalate_when: Link status remains down after confirming no external outage
Loopback test fails and replacement ONT does not restore service
Multiple customers in the same exchange report identical symptoms
notes: Fiber cuts are most often caused by third-party construction or accidental damage. Restoration time depends on access to the splice points and crew availability. Keep the customer updated with any changes from the field team.

title: Nimbus Fibre - Complete Loss of Internet After Service Modification
symptoms: I can't load any websites at all
My router shows no internet light
All devices say they're disconnected from the network
The speed test app reports zero bandwidth

diagnostic_questions.q: Did the customer request a different broadband tier within the past 48 hours?
Is the router's WAN port LED solid amber or off?

steps.text: Open the Customer Management System (CMS) and locate the account; verify the current service tier matches the customer's request.
In the Network Management System (NMS), check the provisioning status flag for the line; it should be 'Active' - if it shows 'Pending' or 'Error', note the code.
Confirm the VLAN ID assigned to the customer's ONT matches the product profile for Nimbus Fibre; mismatched VLANs cause traffic blockage.
Run a downstream signal test from the NMS console to ensure the optical signal is within acceptable levels; record loss and OSNR values.
If the VLAN or status is incorrect, trigger a manual re-provision command for the line, forcing the system to rewrite the profile to the ONT.
After re-provisioning, ask the customer to power-cycle the router (unplug for 10 seconds, plug back in) and verify that the internet light turns green and a ping to 8.8.8.8 succeeds.

escalate_when: Provisioning status remains 'Pending' or returns an error code after re-provisioning
Customer still reports no internet connectivity after the router power-cycle
notes: This scenario is typically caused by a backend provisioning mismatch after a plan upgrade. Ensure all profile IDs are consistent across CMS and NMS before closing the ticket.

title: Nimbus ONT-5G - No Connectivity After Account Hold
symptoms: Websites fail to load at all
All status LEDs on the ONT are dark
Wi-Fi network SSID is missing from device lists
Phone service shows no dial tone
Speed-test app reports 0 kbps

diagnostic_questions.q: Has the customer received a recent bill indicating an overdue balance?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Proceed to verify account hold status

diagnostic_questions.q: When was the last successful internet test performed?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Assume outage may be unrelated to billing

steps.text: Open the Nimbus Billing Portal using the agent console and locate the customer's account by subscriber ID.
Confirm the account shows a "Hold" or "Suspended" status flagged for payment delinquency.
If hold is present, place a temporary "Reinstate" flag and note the transaction ID; this lifts the service block in the provisioning system.
Log into the NMS (Network Management System), locate the ONT-5G device by its serial number, and force a re-registration (clear the "suspended" flag).
Monitor the ONT's LED panel remotely; expect the Power LED to turn solid green, the Sync LED to flash, and the Internet LED to become steady.
Run a remote ping test to a known Nimbus DNS server; a successful reply indicates the data path is restored.

escalate_when: Account status remains "Hold" after attempted reinstatement
ONT fails to change LED state after re-registration
Remote ping test continues to time out
notes: Billing holds must be cleared by Finance before service can be fully restored. Document the transaction ID and inform the customer of any outstanding balance to avoid repeat suspensions.

title: Reduced throughput after monthly allowance is reached
symptoms: Web pages take a long time to load
Video streams constantly buffer
File downloads are much slower than usual
Online games lag or disconnect

diagnostic_questions.q: Has the customer exceeded their monthly data allowance?
Is the customer's current speed test below the advertised rate for their plan?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Look for network outages or hardware problems

steps.text: Open the customer's account in the CRM and pull the data usage report; note the percentage of the monthly cap used. Expected outcome: usage level is displayed.
Access the network management console and locate the fair-use flag for the subscriber's line; verify whether throttling is active. Expected outcome: throttling status is shown (active/inactive).

Run a speed test from the customer's premises (or request the customer to run one) and record the downstream/upstream results. Expected outcome: measured speeds are documented and compared to plan limits.

If throttling is active, calculate the remaining time until the next billing cycle reset and inform the customer of the expected speed restoration date. Expected outcome: customer is aware of when normal speeds will resume.

Offer the customer a data-add-on package or an upgrade to a higher-tier plan to avoid future throttling; document the choice in the ticket. Expected outcome: a mitigation option is provided and recorded.

If the fair-use flag is set but the usage report shows the customer is below the cap, flag the account for manual review and reset the throttle flag if appropriate. Expected outcome: erroneous throttling is cleared.

escalate_when: Throttling flag is active while usage is below the cap
Customer reports intermittent high speeds despite throttling being applied
System error prevents retrieval of usage or throttling status
notes: Fair-use policy applies after 80% of the monthly data allowance is consumed. Throttling reduces speeds to 5 Mbps downstream until the next billing cycle. Document any add-on purchases for billing compliance.

title: Nimbus Mesh - Slow Throughput Caused by Wiring Faults
symptoms: Web pages take a long time to load
Video streams pause frequently
Large file downloads are much slower than usual
Speed test reports only a fraction of the subscribed rate

diagnostic_questions.q: Has any recent work been done on the telephone or coaxial outlets in the premises?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Proceed to inspect the outlet and connected hardware for damage

diagnostic_questions.q: Do all devices on the Mesh network experience the slowdown, or only specific ones?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: If all devices are affected, focus on the backbone wiring
diagnostic_questions.if_no: If only some devices are affected, consider device-specific issues

steps.text: Ask the customer to locate the primary Nimbus Mesh node and the nearest wall plate where the service enters the home.
Visually inspect the wall plate and any inline splitter for cracked, corroded or loose connectors; note any visible damage.
Disconnect the existing splitter and replace it with a known-good Nimbus-approved splitter, ensuring the pins are fully seated.
Using a calibrated cable tester, measure continuity and return loss on the inbound line; replace any cable showing high resistance or excessive loss.
Reconnect the Mesh node, power it on, and run a speed test from a wired device directly attached to the node; record the result.
If the speed matches the plan, re-attach the original splitter to confirm it was the fault; if speeds remain low, proceed to escalation

escalate_when: Speed test remains below 70% of the plan after splitter and cable replacement
Line test shows attenuation greater than 20 dB or intermittent signal loss
notes: Document the serial numbers of any replaced splitters and cables; update the ticket with test results for future reference.

title: Nimbus Fibre - Reduced throughput on high-speed plan
symptoms: Websites take a long time to load
Streaming video constantly buffers
Large file downloads are unusually slow
Online games lag or disconnect

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the customer using a router model released before 2018?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Proceed to check firmware and consider replacement

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the router firmware up to date?

steps.text: Ask the customer for the router make and model (check label or admin page). Expected outcome: Agent knows exact hardware version.
Cross-reference the model against Nimbus Fibre's supported list for the subscribed tier. Expected outcome: Determine if the router can handle the plan's maximum speed.

Log into the router interface and note the firmware version; if it is older than the latest release, walk the customer through the update process. Expected outcome: Router runs the most recent firmware, eliminating software limits.

Inspect the Ethernet cable between the wall outlet and the router; ensure it is Cat5e or higher and free of damage, replace if necessary. Expected outcome: Physical link capable of full gigabit throughput.
Perform a wired speed test directly on a LAN port using a laptop or test device. Expected outcome: Baseline speed measurement without Wi-Fi interference.
If speeds remain low, have the customer connect a known-good, Nimbus-certified router to the same line and repeat the speed test. Expected outcome: Isolate the original router as the limiting factor.
When the test router delivers expected speeds, schedule a hardware upgrade for the customer's router. Expected outcome: Customer receives a router that matches the plan's capacity.
Record all findings, update the ticket with the resolution steps taken, and close the case or hand off if further issues arise.

escalate_when: Speed test remains below 70% of the subscribed rate even after testing with a known-good router
Line fault is detected during diagnostics (e.g., signal loss or high error rate)
Customer's router is on the approved list but still cannot achieve expected speeds
notes: Confirm the customer is on the advertised high-speed tier; many older routers cap at 100 Mbps despite gigabit ports. Recommend Nimbus Fibre-certified routers for optimal performance.
root_cause: router too old for the plan speed

title: Nimbus Mesh - Slow Speeds Due to Excessive Background Traffic
symptoms: Web pages load much slower than usual
Video streams pause or buffer constantly
Online games feel laggy or drop packets
Speed-test results are far below the subscribed rate

diagnostic_questions.q: Are there any devices on the network currently downloading large files or performing software updates?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Proceed to identify the device and advise pausing the transfer
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Ask about streaming or cloud backup activity

diagnostic_questions.q: Do you notice the slowdown only at certain times of day?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Correlate with possible peak-hour usage from other households
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Assume constant background load on the local network

steps.text: Log into the Nimbus Mesh admin portal and open the 'Connected Devices' dashboard.
Sort the device list by current bandwidth usage and note any entries consuming >20% of total capacity.
Contact the customer to confirm whether those high-usage devices are performing intentional tasks (e.g., video rendering, cloud backup).
If the usage is non-essential, guide the customer to pause or schedule the activity for off-peak hours, or enable the built-in QoS profile for 'Low-Priority Traffic'.
After adjustments, run a speed test from a wired client connected to a Mesh node and record the result.
Compare the new speed-test value with the plan's advertised speed; if it meets or exceeds 80% of the plan, close the case, otherwise continue troubleshooting.

escalate_when: Speed test remains below 50% of the subscribed rate after eliminating background traffic
Multiple devices still report the same slowdown despite QoS changes
notes: Heavy background traffic on the home LAN is a common cause of reduced throughput on Nimbus Mesh. Ensure the customer understands how to monitor device usage and leverage QoS settings before escalating.
root_cause: heavy background usage on the home network

title: Optimizing Nimbus Mesh node locations for full-home coverage
symptoms: Internet drops in the bedroom
Streaming stops in the living area
Phone loses connection when moving to the hallway
Web pages load slowly in the study
Smart TV shows 'no internet' message

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the primary Mesh unit positioned inside a cabinet or behind large furniture?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Proceed to recommend relocation to an open area

diagnostic_questions.q: Do you see a signal strength below -70 dBm on any device in the problem area?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Suggest moving the nearest node closer

steps.text: Ask the customer to open the Nimbus app and display the current Wi-Fi heat-map; note the zones with low signal.
Confirm the physical location of the primary Mesh unit and each satellite; ensure they are not inside enclosed spaces, metal cabinets, or directly under appliances.
Measure the RSSI at the primary unit using the app; it should be at least -60 dBm. If lower, relocate the unit to a central, elevated spot away from walls.
For each satellite, check the inter-node link quality (should be > -65 dBm). If the link is weak, move the satellite 1-2 m closer to the primary unit while maintaining line-of-sight.
Identify nearby sources of RF interference (microwave ovens, cordless phones, baby monitors). Advise the customer to keep Mesh nodes at least 1 m away from such devices.
After repositioning, have the customer re-run the heat-map and verify that all rooms now show a signal above -70 dBm.
Document the final node locations and signal readings in the ticket before closing.

escalate_when: Signal remains below -70 dBm in any area after optimal placement
Inter-node link quality stays under -80 dBm despite adjustments
Customer reports persistent dead zones after three relocation attempts
notes: Nimbus Mesh automatically balances traffic; however, physical barriers and interference are the most common reasons for spotty coverage. Ensure the customer understands that moving nodes is preferred over adding additional units unless the home size exceeds the recommended coverage area.

title: Resolving Wi-Fi dead zones caused by lost mesh node pairing on Nimbus ONT-5G
symptoms: Internet works in the living room but disappears in the upstairs bedroom
My phone shows no Wi-Fi signal in the hallway
Streaming stops when I walk into the kitchen
Devices reconnect only after moving back to the main router area

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the secondary mesh node's status LED solid green?
Did the node lose connection after a recent power outage or reboot?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Ask the customer to note the time of outage

diagnostic_questions.q: Can the node be seen in the Nimbus app under 'Connected Devices'?

steps.text: Ask the customer to locate the secondary mesh node and confirm it is plugged into a working outlet; advise them to press the power button until the LED flashes amber, indicating it is booting.
In the Nimbus app, navigate to 'Mesh Management' and select the affected node; note the current status (e.g., 'Disconnected' or 'Error').

If the node shows 'Disconnected', initiate a manual re-pair: press and hold the reset button on the node for 10 seconds until the LED turns blue, then select 'Add Node' in the app and follow the on-screen prompts.
After the node re-appears, verify the back-haul connection by checking that the LED on the node turns solid green and the app displays a 'Strong' link quality.
Ask the customer to perform a quick Wi-Fi speed test in the previously problematic area; confirm that signal strength is now ≥-65 dBm and throughput is within expected limits for their plan.
If signal remains weak, move the node 1-2 feet closer to the primary ONT-5G unit, ensuring no large metal objects or thick walls obstruct the line-of-sight, then repeat step 4.
Document the node's MAC address, firmware version, and the time of re-pair; advise the customer that the node will automatically re-sync with the network over the next 10-15 minutes.
Close the case with a confirmation that Wi-Fi coverage is restored throughout the home; schedule a follow-up call in 48 hours if issues recur.

escalate_when: Node remains offline after manual re-pair attempts
LED stays red or amber despite power cycle
Speed test still shows <-70 dBm in multiple rooms after steps are completed
notes: Nimbus ONT-5G firmware version 3.2.1 introduced a known bug where mesh nodes can lose pairing after an unclean shutdown. Ensure the node's firmware is updated to 3.2.5 during re-pair if the app prompts for an upgrade.

title: Nimbus Mesh - Spotty Wi-Fi due to Device Locked on 2.4 GHz
symptoms: Internet works fine in the living room but drops completely in the bedroom.
Streaming video buffers constantly in one part of the house.
My phone shows no networks when I'm upstairs.
Laptop sees a weak signal and pages take a long time to load.

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the problematic device connected to a network whose SSID indicates a 2.4 GHz band (e.g., ends with '_2G' or shows '2.4 GHz' in Wi-Fi details)?
Does the device's specifications list support for 5 GHz Wi-Fi?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Inform the customer the device is limited to 2.4 GHz.

steps.text: Ask the customer to open the device's Wi-Fi settings and ensure the band selection is set to 'Auto' or '5 GHz preferred' rather than '2.4 GHz only'; note the current setting.
In the Nimbus Mesh mobile app, go to Settings → Advanced → Band Steering and verify it is enabled; if it is disabled, turn it on.

If Band Steering was already enabled, temporarily disable it, then manually connect the device to the 5 GHz SSID (e.g., NimbusMesh_5G) and confirm the device obtains an IP address and internet access.
Instruct the customer to check for and apply any available firmware/driver updates for the device using the manufacturer's update utility or app.
Re-enable Band Steering in the Mesh app and allow the system a few minutes to re-optimize device placement across bands.
From the app, run a Wi-Fi scan on the affected device and verify that the 5 GHz network now appears as an available option.
Ask the customer to move the nearest Mesh node within approximately 10 m of the problem area (e.g., upstairs bedroom) and re-measure signal strength via the app's signal meter.
Document whether the device now connects to the 5 GHz band and reports normal speeds; if it still only sees the 2.4 GHz network, proceed to escalation.

escalate_when: Device continues to connect exclusively to the 2.4 GHz network after all steps.
Multiple devices in the same area are affected and band steering does not resolve the issue.
Firmware update fails or the Mesh app reports errors during band-steering configuration.
notes: Some legacy smartphones, tablets, or IoT gadgets only support 2.4 GHz. If the device is confirmed to lack 5 GHz capability, advise the customer to use a dedicated 2.4 GHz extender or upgrade the hardware.
root_cause: device stuck on the 2.4 GHz band

title: Weak Wi-Fi coverage caused by neighbouring network interference
symptoms: slow internet speed in the bedroom
connection drops when moving to the kitchen
device shows 'no internet' in the upstairs office
signal strength indicator low in the hallway
web pages load very slowly in the living room

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the ONT placed near a window or external wall?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Recommend moving the ONT at least 1 m away from the exterior surface.

diagnostic_questions.q: When scanning the radio environment, do you see many other wireless networks on the same channel?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Suggest changing to a less-congested channel or enabling auto-channel selection.
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Continue with power and band adjustments.

steps.text: Log into the Nimbus ONT-5G admin portal and navigate to the Wi-Fi settings page.
Enable the built-in channel scanner; record the top three least-used 2.4 GHz channels and the least-used 5 GHz channels.
Manually set the 2.4 GHz radio to channel 1, 6, or 11 based on the scan results, and set the 5 GHz radio to a DFS or upper-band channel with minimal overlap.
Reduce the transmit power to 50 % for 2.4 GHz and 70 % for 5 GHz, then re-enable auto-power after 2 minutes to let the ONT recalibrate.
Activate band steering (if available) so dual-band clients are preferentially moved to 5 GHz, reducing contention on the crowded 2.4 GHz band.
Ask the customer to place a client device in the previously problematic area and run a speed test; verify signal strength ≥-65 dBm and sustained throughput ≥10 Mbps.
If performance is still unsatisfactory, advise repositioning the ONT to a more central location away from metal objects and large appliances, then repeat steps 2-6.

escalate_when: Signal remains poor after changing channels and adjusting power
More than five overlapping networks are detected on the selected band
Hardware diagnostics indicate antenna or radio failure
notes: ONT-5G supports dual-band, 2.4 GHz (20/40 MHz) and 5 GHz (20/40/80 MHz). Use DFS channels only if the customer's firmware is up-to-date. Document all channel changes in the ticket for future reference.

title: Incorrect charge after Nimbus Fibre package upgrade - proration discrepancy
symptoms: My monthly bill is higher than usual after I upgraded my service.
I see a charge that looks like I'm paying for two different speeds at once.
The amount on my invoice doesn't match what I was told would be the cost.
I was told the upgrade would be cheaper for the rest of the month, but it isn't.

diagnostic_questions.q: Did the customer change their Nimbus Fibre package during the current billing cycle?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Proceed to verify the change date and billing entries.

diagnostic_questions.q: Is there a separate line item for the previous package and the new package on the same invoice?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Check the dates and amounts for each line.
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Confirm if the system applied a full-month charge.

diagnostic_questions.q: Has the system already applied a credit for the unused days of the old package?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Ensure the credit amount matches the prorated value.

steps.text: Retrieve the customer's account and open the billing history for the current cycle.
Identify the exact date and time the Nimbus Fibre package was changed and note the old and new plan rates.
Compare the invoice line items to the change date; verify whether a prorated charge and a corresponding credit were generated.
Recalculate the correct prorated amount using the formula: (Daily rate of old plan × remaining days) + (Daily rate of new plan × days used) and compare to what was billed.
If the billed amount is higher, create a corrective credit for the difference and attach a note explaining the adjustment.
Update the invoice status to "Corrected", send the revised invoice to the customer, and log the interaction in the case record.

escalate_when: The billing engine fails to generate a prorated credit after manual adjustment.
The discrepancy exceeds $50 or the customer requests a refund beyond a standard credit.
notes: Proration is calculated automatically by the billing system; manual overrides should be documented. Advise customers to schedule future package changes at the start of a billing cycle to avoid similar issues.

title: Duplicate billing entry on Nimbus Mobile invoice
symptoms: My latest bill shows the same amount listed twice.
My bill includes a call I never placed.
There is an extra line item that matches a previous one.
The total I owe is higher than expected for this period.

diagnostic_questions.q: Does the invoice contain two line items with identical dates, amounts, and descriptions?
Is the disputed amount present on the previous month's invoice as well?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Likely a recurring duplicate; continue investigation.
diagnostic_questions.if_no: May be a one-off error; review payment logs.

steps.text: Verify the customer's account number and pull the latest Nimbus Mobile invoice.
Locate the disputed line items and record their transaction/reference IDs.
Cross-reference those IDs with the billing system's transaction log for the same billing cycle.
Determine whether the IDs correspond to the same underlying usage event.
If they are duplicates, apply a corrective credit to the customer's account and add an internal note explaining the adjustment.
Generate and send an updated invoice to the customer, then confirm the issue is resolved.

escalate_when: Unable to find matching transaction IDs in the billing system.
Customer reports the same issue on multiple invoices.
notes: Document the credit amount and reference the original invoice numbers. Ensure the case is logged for audit purposes.

title: Promotional Discount Expired - Billing Dispute for Nimbus Fibre
symptoms: I was charged the full monthly rate this cycle.
My invoice shows a higher amount than usual.
Why am I paying extra for my fibre service?
The bill this month doesn't match my previous statements.
I thought I was still getting the special price.

diagnostic_questions.q: Was the promotional period for the customer's plan listed as ending before the current billing cycle?
Is the customer's account flagged as having an active promotion in the billing system?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Investigate why the promotion wasn't applied.
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Confirm that the regular rate applies.

steps.text: Open the customer's profile in the billing console and pull the most recent invoice; this confirms the amount being disputed.
Navigate to the promotions tab, locate the specific offer tied to the account, and record its start and end dates; this establishes the validity window.
Cross-reference the promotion end date with the start date of the disputed billing period; determines whether the discount should apply.
If the promotion ended before the disputed period, compute the standard monthly charge for that cycle and note any prorated adjustments; prepares the corrected amount.
Update the invoice in the system with the corrected charge, attach an audit note explaining the discount expiry, and trigger a revised bill to be sent to the customer; ensures accurate billing.
Contact the customer, explain the findings, confirm the updated amount, and offer a goodwill gesture if policy permits; completes the interaction and logs closure.

escalate_when: Customer claims the promotion should still be active despite system showing it ended
System records a promotion end date that does not match the contract documentation
Customer requests a retroactive credit for the period after the promotion ended
notes: Document all date checks and calculations in the case notes. If the promotion end date is ambiguous, involve the billing policy team before finalizing the adjustment.

title: Unexpected Penalty on Nimbus Mobile Invoice
symptoms: I was charged extra this month
My bill shows a fee I don't recognize
Why is there an additional amount on my statement?
The invoice total is higher than expected

diagnostic_questions.q: Did the customer's payment post after the due date?
Is the payment record showing a successful transaction?

steps.text: Open the customer's Nimbus Mobile account in the CRM and pull the latest invoice details.
Locate the payment history tab and verify the timestamp of the last payment relative to the invoice due date.
Confirm that the payment was posted successfully and note the exact posting time.
If the payment failed or was rejected, capture the error code and inform the customer that the fee is due to an unpaid balance.
If the payment posted after the due date, reference the Late Payment Policy and calculate the applicable fee.
Explain the fee to the customer, citing the policy clause and the date the payment was received.
Check eligibility for a one-time fee waiver (e.g., first-time occurrence, goodwill) and apply if approved.
Document the interaction, update the case notes with the resolution, and close the ticket.

escalate_when: The customer remains dissatisfied after the waiver is denied
The system shows the payment as posted on time but the fee is still applied
A policy exception is required beyond standard guidelines
notes: All communications should reference the internal Late Payment Policy document (ID: LPP-2024) and use the standard fee-waiver script for consistency.
root_cause: late fee applied after payment delay

title: Nimbus Fibre - Activation pending in provisioning queue
symptoms: My internet hasn't started even though the order was confirmed.
I'm still seeing 'service not active' on my account page.
The welcome email never arrived.
The technician said the line would be live today, but nothing works.
My new plan shows as 'processing' for days.

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the customer's order status showing 'Provisioning - In Progress' in the CRM?
Has the customer received a provisioning confirmation email?
Is the NMS indicating the service as 'Not Yet Activated'?

steps.text: Open the Order Management System, locate the customer's order and confirm product code, address, and start date match the request. Expected outcome: order details are correct.
Retrieve the provisioning ticket ID from the Network Management System and view its current stage. Expected outcome: ticket is in 'Queued' or 'Pending Activation'.
Execute the 'Reset Provisioning Queue' script for the service ID. Expected outcome: ticket status changes to 'Processing'.
Manually re-run the 'Service Activation' job for that ticket. Expected outcome: activation job completes without error.
Check the FTTH port status in the NMS; it should transition to 'Online'. Expected outcome: port shows active and traffic is permitted.
Send a confirmation email to the customer stating the service is now live and include any next-step instructions. Expected outcome: customer receives the email.
Update the CRM status field to 'Active - Service Live'. Expected outcome: account reflects live service.
Record all actions in the case notes and close the ticket if the customer confirms connectivity. Expected outcome: case is documented and resolved.

escalate_when: Ticket remains in 'Queued' after the reset script.
NMS reports hardware fault on the assigned port.
Customer reports no service after all steps are completed.
notes: Applicable to new Nimbus Fibre installations and plan upgrades where the provisioning workflow appears stalled. Do not use a router reboot as the sole remedy; follow the full queue-reset procedure.

title: Incorrect Nimbus Mobile Plan Provisioned During Activation
symptoms: My data allowance is much lower than what I signed up for
I'm being billed for a different service tier
Features like unlimited calls aren't available
The app shows a plan I never chose

diagnostic_questions.q: Does the customer's account summary display the plan they expected?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Check the provisioning record for mismatched plan.

diagnostic_questions.q: Was a confirmation email or SMS sent with the new plan details?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Compare the email details with the system record.

diagnostic_questions.q: Is there an open change request ticket for this account?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Link the ticket and follow its notes.

steps.text: Retrieve the customer's MSISDN and account ID from the CRM system.
Pull the provisioning log from the NMS for the activation timestamp.
Compare the plan code in the log with the plan the customer purchased using the product catalog.
If a mismatch is found, run the "Plan Reconcile" script to withdraw the incorrect plan and apply the correct one.
Verify the new plan appears in the billing system and the mobile app within five minutes.
Notify the customer, confirm data/voice limits are correct, and close the ticket with full documentation.

escalate_when: Provisioning log returns an error code and cannot be edited
After re-provisioning, the customer's app still shows the wrong plan
notes: Use the latest product-catalog version when matching plan codes. Record the original erroneous plan code for audit purposes. If the NMS API is unavailable, route to the platform team.

title: Port-in failure during Nimbus Fibre activation
symptoms: My new broadband isn't live yet
The system says my service is pending
I was told my phone number isn't available on the new line
I get an error saying the number can't be moved

diagnostic_questions.q: Has the customer provided the correct Porting Authorization Code (PAC) from the previous carrier?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Proceed to verify the PAC format in the system.
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Ask customer to obtain the correct PAC and retry.

diagnostic_questions.q: Does the original carrier show the number as active and eligible for porting?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Inform customer they must cancel the existing service first.

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the port request status in the provisioning portal showing 'Rejected'?

steps.text: Open the customer record and confirm the full phone number and service address are entered correctly in the Nimbus CRM.
Navigate to the Provisioning Dashboard, locate the port-in request, and note the current status and any reason code displayed.
Cross-check the PAC entered in the system against the code supplied by the customer; correct any mismatches.
Verify there are no outstanding balances, active contracts, or service blocks on the donor carrier that would block the port.
If any data issues were found, amend the request and resubmit the port-in through the portal, capturing the new transaction ID.
Monitor the request for a status change to 'Accepted'; once accepted, enable the Nimbus Fibre activation flag and schedule the service cut-over.
Send a confirmation email to the customer with the expected activation time and any next-step instructions.

escalate_when: Port request remains rejected after two resubmissions
Donor carrier returns a 'Number not eligible' response
Provisioning system error code cannot be cleared by agent
notes: Ensure all customer-provided identifiers are double-checked; a single digit error in the PAC is a common cause of rejection. Document any reason codes received for trend analysis.

title: Missed Installation Appointment - Service Not Activated for Nimbus Mobile
symptoms: My new mobile service still shows as inactive.
I was told my line would be ready today, but nothing works.
The technician never arrived and I can't use my phone.
I received a welcome email but the service isn't usable yet.

diagnostic_questions.q: Has the customer received a scheduled appointment confirmation email or SMS?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Proceed to verify the appointment status in the system.
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Ask the customer to provide the confirmation details or note that none was sent.

diagnostic_questions.q: Does the provisioning system show the service as 'Pending Installation'?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Check the appointment log for a missed visit.
diagnostic_questions.if_no: The service may be stuck in another stage; investigate further.

steps.text: Retrieve the customer's account and verify the activation request date.
Open the Service Provisioning Dashboard and locate the appointment record for the customer.
Confirm whether the appointment status is marked 'No Show' or 'Cancelled by Technician'.
If marked 'No Show', contact the scheduling team to arrange a new installation slot within the next 2 business days, and update the appointment status to 'Rescheduled'.
Update the provisioning status to 'Scheduled - Awaiting Installation' and trigger an automated confirmation message to the customer.
Document the interaction in the case notes, set a follow-up reminder for 24 hours after the new appointment, and close the ticket if the customer acknowledges the new schedule.

escalate_when: Customer reports multiple missed appointments in the last 30 days.
System shows the appointment as completed but the customer still has no service.
The scheduling team cannot provide a new slot within the SLA.
notes: Applies to Nimbus Mobile new activations, plan changes, or number ports that require a field technician. Ensure all timestamps are logged for audit compliance.

title: Diagnosing ONT hardware fault on Nimbus ONT-5G
symptoms: No lights are lit on the white box.
Internet connection is completely missing.
Speed test shows 0 Mbps.
The device makes no clicking or blinking sounds.

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the power LED on?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Proceed to check the fiber LED.

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the fiber (PON) LED steady or flashing?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Inspect the fiber connector for damage.

diagnostic_questions.q: Has the ONT been power-cycled in the last 5 minutes?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Ask customer to power-cycle and report.

steps.text: Verify that the ONT is receiving mains power by plugging a known-good lamp into the same outlet; expected outcome: lamp lights, confirming outlet is live.
Confirm the power adapter is functional by measuring its output voltage (12 V DC) with a multimeter; expected outcome: reading close to 12 V.
Inspect and reseat the fiber optic connector (SC/APC); look for dust or bent fibers; expected outcome: clean connection and fiber LED changes to steady.
Access the ONT web UI (192.168.1.1) and run the built-in diagnostics; expected outcome: diagnostic page reports hardware status or displays error codes.
If diagnostics report a hardware error, replace the ONT with a spare unit from inventory; expected outcome: new unit powers up, LEDs behave normally, internet restores.
Re-provision the replaced ONT in the NMS so it registers and syncs downstream; expected outcome: device shows as online with proper sync status.
Perform a speed test to verify service levels; expected outcome: speeds are within the agreed SLA.

escalate_when: ONT self-test returns a hardware error code.
Power LED remains off after confirming outlet and adapter are functional.
Multiple downstream ports on the same cabinet are reporting similar failures.
notes: Document the hardware replacement in the ticket, update the asset inventory, and schedule a field engineer visit only if a spare ONT is not available or the issue recurs after replacement.

title: Nimbus Mesh - Device temperature causing connectivity issues
symptoms: Wi-Fi drops after the unit feels warm
LED indicator flickers or turns amber when the box is hot
Internet speed slows dramatically after a few hours of use
The mesh unit powers off unexpectedly during heavy traffic
Room temperature near the device seems higher than usual

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the surface of the Mesh unit noticeably warm or hot to the touch?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Proceed to ventilation and placement checks

diagnostic_questions.q: Do the status LEDs show intermittent amber or red flashes?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Log the event and continue with thermal mitigation steps

steps.text: Ask the customer to place the Mesh unit on a flat, non-carpeted surface with at least 10 cm clearance on all sides to improve airflow; expect better heat dissipation.
Instruct the customer to power off the unit, unplug it, and inspect the vent openings for dust or debris; cleaning should reveal unobstructed vents.
Verify ambient room temperature is below 30 °C; if higher, recommend relocating the unit to a cooler area or improving room ventilation.
Check the firmware version via the Nimbus app and, if outdated, guide the customer through a firmware update; updated firmware may include thermal management improvements.
Ask the customer to temporarily disconnect non-essential devices from the Mesh network to reduce processing load; monitor if temperature rise slows.
If the unit remains hot after cleaning, proper placement, and load reduction, schedule a hardware replacement; the expectation is that the new unit will operate within normal temperature range.

escalate_when: Device temperature stays above 45 °C after cleaning and repositioning
Frequent disconnections or power-offs continue despite all mitigation steps
notes: Repeated thermal stress can degrade internal components and lead to premature failure. Document the temperature readings and steps taken in the ticket. If a replacement is issued, log the serial number and arrange for proper disposal of the faulty unit.

title: Nimbus ONT-5G Power Adapter Fault
symptoms: No indicator lights are illuminated
The unit remains completely dark
Internet service is unavailable despite the line being active
The cable attached feels unusually warm

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the wall outlet delivering voltage?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Proceed to test the ONT with a known good adapter.
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Advise customer to try a different outlet or check home wiring.

diagnostic_questions.q: Are any LEDs on the device lit?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Issue may be elsewhere; continue troubleshooting.
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Likely power delivery problem; replace adapter.

steps.text: Verify that the wall outlet is live using a voltage tester; expected reading 110-120 V AC.
Disconnect the existing power cable from the ONT and inspect the connector for damage or discoloration.
Connect a known-good Nimbus-compatible power adapter to the ONT and observe LED status.
If LEDs illuminate, confirm internet connectivity; if not, note any fault code displayed.
Replace the original adapter with the spare unit and re-secure the cable; document serial numbers.
Perform a quick sync test by sending a ping from the management console; expect <50 ms response.

escalate_when: LEDs remain off after connecting a verified good adapter
Device reports a hardware fault code after replacement
notes: Keep a stock of verified good adapters on hand for rapid swaps. Record adapter serial numbers and any observed fault codes for trend analysis.

title: Nimbus Mesh - Intermittent connectivity due to physical link failure
symptoms: Internet connection drops every few minutes
No indicator lights on the Mesh node
Web pages load extremely slowly
Device shows 'No Internet' status in the app

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the Ethernet line firmly seated in the Mesh unit and the wall outlet?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Ask customer to unplug and re-plug the line firmly

diagnostic_questions.q: Do any LEDs on the Mesh unit display amber or red?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Note the error indication and continue

steps.text: Ask the customer to locate the Ethernet line that connects the Nimbus Mesh unit to the wall socket and visually inspect it for kinks, fraying, or exposed conductors.
Instruct the customer to disconnect the line from both ends, then reconnect it ensuring a solid click in the connectors.
If the issue persists, provide a spare Ethernet line and have the customer replace the existing one, then verify link lights on the Mesh unit.
Should the problem remain, direct the customer to connect the Mesh unit to an alternative wall socket using the same spare line to rule out a faulty wall interface.
If connectivity is restored on the alternate socket, label the original socket as defective and schedule a technician visit.
If the problem still exists after cable swap and alternate socket test, run the built-in diagnostics from the support portal to capture error codes for further analysis.

escalate_when: The Ethernet line shows visible damage such as cuts or exposed wires
Link lights remain off after swapping to a known-good line and using a different wall socket
notes: Document the serial number of the Mesh unit and the exact error code from diagnostics before escalation. Ensure the customer is advised not to use the damaged line again.

title: VoLTE service not active on Nimbus Mobile SIM
symptoms: Calls connect but audio cuts out after a few seconds
Unable to place calls while the phone shows a 4G icon
SMS messages are delayed or not delivered
Mobile data falls back to 3G even in LTE-covered areas

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the device displaying a 4G/LTE signal icon?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Check network coverage or device compatibility

diagnostic_questions.q: Has the customer recently swapped the SIM into a new device?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Verify device supports VoLTE and provisioning may be needed

steps.text: Confirm the handset model is listed as VoLTE-compatible in the Nimbus Mobile device compatibility matrix; outcome: compatibility verified or not.
Log into the Nimbus provisioning portal and review the customer's account for VoLTE status; outcome: see whether VoLTE is currently disabled.
If VoLTE is disabled, enable the VoLTE flag for the SIM and save the changes; outcome: VoLTE activation flag set to active.
Guide the customer to Settings → Network → Advanced and toggle the "VoLTE calls" option on; outcome: device is set to use VoLTE when available.
Ask the customer to power-cycle the device (full reboot); outcome: device re-registers with the network using the new provisioning.
After reboot, verify that a VoLTE/HD Voice icon appears and that voice calls and mobile data remain on 4G; outcome: issue resolved if icon present and performance normal.

escalate_when: VoLTE remains inactive after provisioning and device reboot
Customer reports persistent call drops or data fallback despite completing all steps
notes: Older handset firmware may lack VoLTE support; advise a software update before provisioning. If provisioning fails repeatedly, a SIM replacement may be required.
root_cause: VoLTE not enabled on the SIM

title: Roaming service not active on Nimbus Mobile
symptoms: Cannot place or receive calls while abroad
Mobile data stays disconnected in a foreign country
Text messages never arrive after traveling overseas
Phone shows "No Service" after crossing the border

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the subscriber currently located outside their home coverage area?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Explain that roaming issues only occur abroad

diagnostic_questions.q: Does the device display the home network name instead of a local carrier?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Suggest they manually select a local network and re-check

diagnostic_questions.q: Has roaming been previously enabled on this account?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Verify current status in the system

steps.text: Open the Nimbus CRM, locate the subscriber's profile using MSISDN or account number.
Navigate to the 'Services' tab and check the status of the 'International Roaming' toggle.
If the toggle is off, click to enable it, select the appropriate roaming package, and save the changes; system should return a confirmation code.
Ask the customer to power-cycle the device or toggle Airplane Mode on for 30 seconds, then turn it off to force a network re-registration.
Instruct the customer to go to Settings → Network → Network Operators and select "Automatic" or manually choose a local operator; verify that the signal bars display the foreign carrier.
Confirm with the customer that calls, SMS, and data now work; if not, run a quick network test from the CRM to log the current registration status.

escalate_when: The account does not have a roaming-eligible plan or quota
System returns an error code when attempting to enable roaming
notes: Applicable to all Nimbus Mobile post-paid and prepaid lines. Ensure the roaming package matches the customer's travel region to avoid unexpected charges.

title: Nimbus Mobile - Service unavailable due to incomplete SIM activation
symptoms: Calls drop as soon as I dial
Cannot send or receive text messages
Mobile data never connects
Phone stays on 'Searching…' with no bars
No network appears in the status bar

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the SIM card seated firmly in the device's slot?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Ask customer to re-insert the SIM and verify it clicks into place

diagnostic_questions.q: Has the customer received the activation SMS from Nimbus after the SIM was inserted?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Check provisioning status in the system
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Resend activation SMS and note timestamp

diagnostic_questions.q: Does the device show the correct IMSI and ICCID in the device info screen?
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Suggest swapping the SIM into another compatible device to rule out a defective card

steps.text: Open the Nimbus Mobile provisioning portal and locate the customer's account using the MSISDN or ICCID
Verify the SIM status field - it should read 'Active'. If it shows 'Pending' or 'Failed', note the timestamp
If status is 'Pending', trigger a manual activation push from the portal and record the activation ID
Ask the customer to power-cycle the handset (turn off, wait 30 seconds, turn on) and then check network registration
Confirm that the device now registers on the correct LTE/5G band and that voice and data services are reachable
If registration still fails, run a remote AT command (AT+CREG?) to read the network registration state and capture any error codes
Log any error codes and, if they indicate a provisioning mismatch, submit a back-end sync request to refresh the SIM profile

escalate_when: SIM remains in 'Pending' or 'Failed' state after manual activation attempt
Customer still cannot register to any network after remote AT command shows registration error
Error codes returned correspond to profile mismatch (e.g., +CME ERROR: 515)
notes: Document the activation ID and timestamps in the ticket. If the SIM works in another device, the issue may be device-specific and should be handed off to the handset support team.

title: Nimbus Mobile - Weak Coverage at Customer Premises
symptoms: calls drop after a few seconds
texts fail to send or receive
mobile data is painfully slow or times out
no signal bars appear even though the phone is on

diagnostic_questions.q: Is the device showing any network bars in the status bar?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Proceed to check signal strength via field test mode
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Advise to move to a different spot and re-check

diagnostic_questions.q: Has the customer experienced the same issue in other locations (e.g., home, work, outdoors)?
diagnostic_questions.if_yes: Proceed to verify SIM and device settings
diagnostic_questions.if_no: Consider a localized coverage issue and suggest alternative indoor positioning

diagnostic_questions.q: Are there any known network incidents reported for the area?

steps.text: Ask the customer to open the device's field test mode (e.g., *3001#12345#* on iOS or dial *#*#4636#*#* on Android) and note the reported signal strength (RSRP) and signal quality (SINR). Expected outcome: numeric values that can be compared to the minimum acceptable thresholds (e.g., RSRP > -110 dBm, SINR > 0 dB).

If the values are below thresholds, instruct the customer to relocate the device a few meters away from walls, windows, or metal objects and repeat the measurement. Expected outcome: improvement in RSRP/SINR or confirmation that the environment is the limiting factor.

Verify that the SIM card is seated correctly: power off the device, remove the SIM, inspect for dust, re-insert, and power on. Expected outcome: device registers on the network and displays at least one bar if the SIM is functional.
Check the device's network mode settings (e.g., LTE/5G preferred, 4G/3G fallback). Ensure it is not locked to an unavailable band. Expected outcome: device can lock onto the strongest available cell.

Run a network reset: Settings → General Management → Reset → Reset Network Settings. Expected outcome: all saved network configurations are cleared and the device attempts a fresh cell search, potentially improving connectivity.

Consult the internal coverage map for the customer's address and cross-reference with any recent tower maintenance logs. Expected outcome: identification of a known weak spot or ongoing maintenance that could explain the issue.

If after steps 1-6 the signal remains below acceptable levels and the customer still reports issues, advise the customer to use a signal-boosting accessory (e.g., a certified external antenna or a femtocell) as a temporary mitigation. Expected outcome: measurable increase in signal strength or at least a stable connection for voice/data.
Document the measured values, actions taken, and the customer's final status in the ticket before closing or escalating. Expected outcome: clear audit trail for future reference.

escalate_when: Signal strength stays below -115 dBm after relocation and network reset
Customer experiences identical issues at multiple, unrelated locations
A network outage or maintenance is confirmed for the area
notes: Weak coverage is often site-specific; ensure the agent records exact RSRP/SINR numbers for trend analysis. Do not suggest a full device replacement unless a hardware fault is proven after all network-related steps.
root_cause: weak coverage at the customer's location
